⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha and under rapid, breaking development. This page describes a moving target and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release — treat everything here as provisional, and do not rely on it for a production deployment.

This page maps the MediaMTX streaming stack as pvarki/opendefence-platform deploys it: what runs inside the mtx-server pod in namespace app-mtx, how every stream publish and view is authenticated through the platform, and which port carries which protocol. It is for operators and developers reading or changing k8s/app-mtx/; for what the product does for end users, see What the MediaMTX integration is. Throughout, <domain> is the deployment host (written {domain} in diagrams), localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi locally.

Pod anatomy

Everything lives in one Deployment, mtx-server (1 replica, strategy Recreate — a redeploy drops all live streams), running under ServiceAccount mtx, which is what gives the pod its Linkerd identity mtx.app-mtx.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local. The pod is Linkerd-injected, but the media listeners are excluded from the mesh via config.linkerd.io/skip-inbound-ports: "1936,8322,8890,9888,9889,9996,9997" — only the HTTP ports (8005 API, 8080 UI) pass through the proxy. The pieces fit together like this:

Container Image Ports Role
mtxrmapi-prep-dirs (init) busybox — creates /data/persistent/public and /data/persistent/private on the mtx-data PVC, chmod 700 on private
mediamtx bluenviron/mediamtx:1.12.3 1936, 8322, 8890 tcp+udp, 9888, 9889, 9996, 9997 the streaming engine; TLS on every listener except SRT

mtxrmapi ghcr.io/pvarki/mediamtx-integration:1.6.2-260707 8005 integration API: auth callback, platform wiring, writes the UI files nginx serves

Configuration and credentials, all declarative:

  • mediamtx.yml comes from the mediamtx-config-files ConfigMap (generated from k8s/app-mtx/base/files/mediamtx.yml), mounted read-only at /mediamtx.yml. Overlay-level tweaks ride in the mtx-config ConfigMap as MediaMTX env overrides: MTX_RTSPTRANSPORTS=tcp (no RTP-over-UDP through the Service) and MTX_WEBRTCADDITIONALHOSTS=mtx.<domain> so WebRTC clients get a reachable host in ICE candidates.
  • mtxrmapi is configured with env prefix RMMTX_. The mtx-secrets Secret is injected wholesale via envFrom with that prefix; database credentials come from the CNPG-generated mtx-postgres-app Secret as RMMTX_DATABASE_{HOST,DATABASE,USER,PASSWORD}. RMMTX_RMCN pins the Linkerd identity mtxrmapi will accept as rmapi (rmapi.opendefence-system.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local, with MTLS_TRUST_L5D=true), and RMMTX_API_URL=https://mtx.<domain>:9997 points it at MediaMTX's own TLS control API.
  • mtx-secrets is an ExternalSecret whose three keys — API_PASSWORD, SRT_PUB_PASSWORD, SRT_READ_PASSWORD — are generated in-cluster (see Data & secrets for the generator pattern). Publishing and reading get separate SRT credentials.
  • TLS for the MediaMTX listeners (every protocol except SRT, which has no TLS mode) comes from the mtx-tls Secret, mounted at /le_certs/rasenmaeher/ as privkey.pem/fullchain.pem. Locally the mtx Certificate is issued by the internal intermediate-ca-issuer; in cloud by letsencrypt-http01-production. The same Secret terminates the Traefik route for mtx.<domain>, so the API hostname and the raw media ports present the same certificate.
  • State: CNPG Cluster mtx-postgres (ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.3, database mtx, owner mtx, 1Gi, ssl_min_protocol_version: TLSv1.2) and PVC mtx-data (1Gi, RWO) at /data/persistent. Both are single-instance with no backups configured (Data & secrets).

Stream authentication

MediaMTX itself holds no user list. mediamtx.yml sets authMethod: http with authHTTPAddress: http://mtx-server-internal.app-mtx.svc.cluster.local:8005/api/v1/mediamtx/auth, so every connect, publish and read — on every protocol — triggers an HTTP callback to mtxrmapi, which allows or denies it against the platform-managed credentials (the generated mtx-secrets passwords and its own records in mtx-postgres). This is the mechanism that extends Deploy App's identity control to the media plane even though the media ports bypass the Traefik/mTLS edge entirely. A publish followed by a view looks like this:

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Pub as Publisher
  participant MTX as MediaMTX
  participant RM as mtxrmapi
  participant View as Viewer
  Pub->>MTX: RTMPS connect on 1936 with stream path and credentials
  MTX->>RM: POST /api/v1/mediamtx/auth (action publish, path, user, ip)
  Note over RM: checks platform-issued credentials
  alt allowed
    RM-->>MTX: 200 OK
    MTX-->>Pub: publish accepted, path goes live
  else denied
    RM-->>MTX: error
    MTX-->>Pub: connection rejected
  end
  View->>MTX: HLS request on 9888 for the same path
  MTX->>RM: POST /api/v1/mediamtx/auth (action read)
  RM-->>MTX: 200 OK
  MTX-->>View: low-latency HLS segments over TLS

blocks.html:
Two consequences: the auth callback stays inside the pod's own Service (loopback via mtx-server-internal), so stream admission keeps working even if the platform edge is briefly unhappy; and because publish and read are separate actions with separate SRT passwords, handing someone view access does not let them inject video.

Two Services, two planes

The stack deliberately splits HTTP traffic (through Traefik, subject to edge mTLS) from raw media traffic (straight to the pod, TLS terminated by MediaMTX itself):

Service Type Ports Reached via
mtx-server-internal ClusterIP 8005 (mtxrmapi), 8080 (UI) IngressRoute mtx: mtx.<domain>/api → 8005, TLSOption mtls-strict + middleware mtls-chain-with-legacy; IngressRoute mtx-ui: mtls.<domain>/ui/mtx → 8080, mtls-optional
mtx-server NodePort (local) / LoadBalancer (cloud, allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false) 1936, 8322, 8890 tcp+udp, 9888, 9889, 9996, 9997 direct, bypassing Traefik
mtx-server-debug NodePort — local overlay only 9998 (metrics), 9999 (pprof) direct, for scraping/profiling from the developer host

The integration API route is mtls-strict: only clients presenting a platform-issued certificate reach mtxrmapi from outside, and the callsign middleware chain applies (see Edge mTLS & callsign checks). Locally the raw Services pin fixed NodePorts equal to the port numbers; in cloud they become LoadBalancer ports on the cluster's external IP — see Ingress & network edge for the exposure map. In the local overlay the Linkerd skip-list is extended with 9998/9999 so debug scrapes from outside the mesh work too. The port map by protocol family:

blocks.html:
The grouping shows each port's primary role — RTSP, RTMP, SRT and WebRTC can technically carry both directions, but every direction on every port goes through the same auth callback. Plain-text variants are off: rtmpEncryption and rtspEncryption are strict, so the unencrypted 1935/8554 listeners are never exposed. Port 9996 is MediaMTX's recording-playback server, and doubles as the product URI the platform advertises (https://mtx.<domain>:9996/). The 9997 control API is how mtxrmapi manages the engine (RMMTX_API_URL); 9998/9999 exist only where mtx-server-debug does.

Platform integration

MediaMTX follows the standard product wiring described in Integration pattern — this section only records the MTX-specific values.

On the core side, rmapi's product registry (kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init.json) contains the mtx entry: api = http://mtx-server-internal.app-mtx.svc.cluster.local:8005/, uri = https://mtx.<domain>:9996/, and certcn = mtx.app-mtx.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local. On the product side, mtxrmapi mounts its own kraftwerk-init.json at /pvarki, pointing back at rasenmaeher.mtls.base_uri = http://rmapi.opendefence-system.svc.cluster.local:8000/ with certcn = rmapi.opendefence-system.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local (duplicated as env RMMTX_RMCN). How this mutual pinning works is covered in Service mesh (Linkerd).

The remaining glue: /ca_public mounts the trust-manager ca-bundle ConfigMap (ca-cert.pem) so the integration can hand out the deployment CA; a container-init.sh is mounted for contract-compatibility with the other products, but MTX's copy (k8s/app-mtx/base/scripts/container-init.sh) is a no-op stub — it just echoes that no container init is required, and carries a TODO to delete it once the legacy Docker Compose stack is deprecated. mtxrmapi also follows the standard readiness contract on /api/v1/healthcheck (port 8005) — see Integration pattern.
